requirements.text: Limit of two future routine GP appointments per patient: The portal shall not permit a patient to hold more than two future routine GP appointments at the same time across all sites.
Exemptions from the two-appointment limit: The two-appointment limit shall not apply to nurse reviews, immunisations or physiotherapy.
Minimum two-hour lead time for bookings: The portal shall not allow a booking that starts less than two hours from the current time.

Carer booking of childhood immunisations within age range: Childhood immunisation appointments shall only be bookable by a carer for a dependant whose age is within the range set for that immunisation type in the PMS.

Reason-for-appointment free-text field: Before confirming a booking the portal shall ask the patient to state the reason for the appointment in a free-text field of up to 200 characters and shall pass it to the PMS with the booking.
Notice that reason field is not monitored: The portal shall tell patients that the reason-for-appointment field is not monitored and that urgent problems must be telephoned in.

Urgent-problem warning on every booking screen: The portal shall show a clear warning on every booking screen that it must not be used for urgent medical problems, including the clinic telephone number and the national urgent care number.
Confirmation only after PMS accepts booking: When a booking is confirmed the portal shall write it to the PMS and shall show the patient a confirmation only after the PMS has accepted it.
Handling PMS unavailability during booking: If the PMS is unavailable, the booking shall be handled appropriately.
Patient cancellation up to two hours before appointment: A patient shall be able to cancel an appointment through the portal up to two hours before its start time.

Moving appointment to another slot of same type: A patient shall be able to move an appointment to another slot of the same appointment type, and the original slot shall be released only once the new booking has been accepted by the PMS.
Cancellation reason selection: The portal shall ask a patient who cancels to choose a reason from a list maintained by the practice managers.

Telephone-booked appointments visible and cancellable in portal: Appointments booked by telephone shall be visible in the portal and shall be cancellable by the patient in the same way as appointments booked online.
Receptionist view of portal account status: Receptionists shall be able to see, for any patient, whether the patient has a portal account and whether it is locked.
No local appointment book copy in portal: The portal shall not keep its own copy of the appointment book; every availability search and booking shall be made against the PMS.
Automatic waiting-list offer for cancelled slots: A cancelled slot shall be offered automatically to patients on the waiting list who said they could attend at that time.
Practice manager control of online-bookable appointment types: Practice managers shall be able to mark or unmark each appointment type at their own site as bookable online.
Online-bookable setting propagation within fifteen minutes: The change to an appointment type's online-bookable status shall take effect in the portal within fifteen minutes.

Front-desk daily online activity list: Front-desk staff shall be able to see a list of the day's online bookings, cancellations and waiting list offers for their site, including the reason for appointment given by each patient.
Suspend online booking for one clinician by date range: Front-desk staff shall be able to suspend online booking for a single clinician for a date range without changing the PMS rota.

Monthly site reporting of online and telephone activity: The portal shall provide a monthly report for each site showing the number of appointments booked, moved and cancelled online, the number of reminders sent, and the number of missed appointments for online and telephone bookings separately.
PMS as system of record for appointments: The PMS shall remain the system of record for appointments; the portal shall read availability from the PMS and write bookings back to it.

First-release scope exclusions: The first release shall exclude video consultations, repeat prescription requests, access to medical records or test results, online payment for travel vaccines, and booking with external providers such as hospital outpatient departments.
Urgent and same-day appointments telephone-only in first release: Urgent and same-day appointments shall remain telephone-only in the first release.
No symptom checker or clinical advice in portal: The portal shall not offer a symptom checker or any form of clinical advice.

requirements.text: Calculate liability limit from lost/damaged weight: The application shall calculate the limit of liability for each consignment from the weight of the goods lost or damaged and the per-kilogram limit in the claimant's terms.

Use declared value as liability limit when charge paid: Where the claimant declared a value for the consignment and paid the declared value charge, the limit of liability shall be the declared value instead of the per-kilogram limit.
Apply special terms liability limits: Where special terms apply, the application shall use the limits in the special terms.
Restrict liability limit overrides: A handler shall not be able to override the calculated limit of liability without the approval of the claims operations manager.

Calculate amount payable as lower of loss value and limit less salvage: The amount payable for a consignment shall be the lower of the proven value of the loss and the limit of liability, less any salvage value recovered from damaged goods.
Show step-by-step payable calculation to handler: The application shall show the handler how the amount payable was calculated, step by step.
Include calculation explanation in settlement letter: The same step-by-step calculation explanation shall be included in the settlement letter to the claimant.
Exclude consequential losses under standard conditions: Consequential losses, such as lost profit or the cost of a missed production run, shall not be payable under the standard conditions.
Prevent consequential loss inclusion unless special terms allow: The application shall prevent a handler from including consequential losses in the amount payable unless the special terms allow them.
Register claims from multiple intake channels: A handler shall be able to register a claim from an email, a telephone note passed on by customer service, or a completed claim form.
Record claim notification channel and timestamp: The application shall record the channel and the date and time the claim was first notified.
Require consignment note number at registration: The application shall require the consignment note number when a claim is registered.

Retrieve consignment details from tracking system: The application shall retrieve the consignment's details from the operational tracking system, including collection and delivery dates, depots passed through, recorded exceptions and proof of delivery.

Register claim with unverified consignment when number not found: If the consignment note number cannot be found in the tracking system, the handler shall be able to register the claim with the consignment marked as unverified.
Prevent payment on unverified consignments: The application shall prevent any payment on a claim whose consignment has not been verified.
Allow one claim to cover multiple consignments: A single claim shall be able to cover several consignments for the same claimant.
Record loss type and claimed amount per consignment: The application shall record the loss type and the amount claimed separately for each consignment on a claim.

Warn about existing claims for a consignment: The application shall warn the handler when a new claim is registered for a consignment that already has an open or closed claim, and shall show the existing claim.
Meet claims desk availability target: The application shall be available during the claims desks' working hours, 7am to 7pm on working days, at least 99.5% of the time.
Support 40 concurrent users within three-second page load: The application shall support at least 40 concurrent users without any page taking more than three seconds to load.
Support home working via standard remote access: The application shall be usable by handlers working from home through the company's standard remote access arrangements.
Apply 14-day damage or shortage notice period: Notice of damage or shortage must be given within 14 days of delivery.
Apply 28-day loss notice period: Notice of loss must be given within 28 days of the expected delivery date.
Issue documents reminder after 21 days: A documents reminder is issued 21 days after the document request.
Close claim as abandoned after reminder: A claim is closed as abandoned 21 days after the documents reminder.
Raise recovery time-limit alert before expiry: A recovery time-limit alert is raised 14 days before expiry.

Define first release claim scope and exclusions: The first release shall cover claims for loss, damage, shortage and delay from business customers on the domestic road network, and shall exclude international shipments and the consumer parcel service.

Provide first release end-to-end claims capabilities: The first release shall cover registration of claims, document collection, liability assessment, calculation of the amount payable, approval, payment instruction, closure, recovery from subcontracted hauliers, preparation of insurance claims, customer notifications and management reporting.

requirements.text: Support seven grant programmes: The system shall support all seven grant programmes, each with its own purpose, budget and eligibility rules.
Record funding rounds: The system shall record each funding round with an opening date, a closing date, a budget and a set of assessment criteria.
Support invitation-only and open rounds: The system shall support rounds that are by invitation only as well as rounds open to any eligible organisation.
Ward Member Grants open all year: Ward Member Grants shall be open all year rather than run as rounds, until each elected member's allocation is spent.

Support full grant lifecycle: The system shall support the full grant lifecycle: programme and round set-up, applicant registration, eligibility checking, application, assessment, decision, grant agreement, payment, variation, monitoring and closure.
Auditor read-only access: Auditors (internal and external) shall have read-only access to the system.
Programme-specific rules isolated by programme: The system shall allow programme-specific rules (Appendix A) to be applied for the programme concerned without affecting other programmes.

Register an organisation: A person shall be able to register an organisation by giving its name, address, legal form, charity or company number if it has one, and details of at least two people connected with it who are not related to each other.

Check charity or company number against public register: Where a charity or company number is given, the system shall check it against the public register and show the officer any difference between the registered name and address and those entered.

Prevent duplicate organisation registration by charity or company number: The system shall prevent registration of an organisation whose charity or company number is already held on another organisation record, and shall direct the person to request access to the existing record.

Multiple users per organisation with peer approval: An organisation record shall be able to have several users, and the organisation's existing users shall approve any request by a new user to join it.

Grants officer can add user when no approvers remain: Where an organisation has no remaining users able to approve a join request, a grants officer shall be able to add a user after verifying that person's connection with the organisation.
Authentication by user type: Council users shall sign in with the council's single sign-on; applicants and external assessors shall sign in with an email address, a password and a second factor.

Remove mistaken personal data from an application: Personal data about applicants' service users included in an application by mistake shall be removable by a grants officer without deleting the rest of the application.

Retention and deletion of grant records: The system shall retain records of approved grants for seven years after the grant is closed and records of declined applications for two years after the decision, and shall then delete them.
Equality information optional and segregated: Equality information given by applicants shall be optional, kept separately from the application, and not visible to assessors or decision-makers.
Prevent payment before grant agreement signed: The system shall prevent any payment on a grant being made before the grant agreement is signed.

Generate grant agreement on approval: When a grant is approved, the system shall generate a grant agreement from the programme template including the amount, the purpose, any conditions set by the decision-maker, the payment schedule and the monitoring requirements.
Electronic signature by grant recipient: The grant recipient shall sign the grant agreement electronically through the system.
Two signatories for grants over 5,000: For grants over 5,000, the grant agreement shall be signed by two people connected with the organisation.
No payment until recipient signs and council countersigns: No payment shall be made on a grant until the agreement has been signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.
Lapse unsigned grant offers: An offer of a grant shall lapse if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time, and the amount shall be returned to the round's budget.

Grants system instructs but does not make payments: The grants system shall instruct payments but shall not make them; the finance system remains the system of record for payments and the council's bank account.
Council website CMS hosts public programme pages: The council's website content management system shall continue to host the public pages about each programme.
